description: We are Space Beatles, a team of students, PhD researchers, and lecturers from Cherkasy State Technological University, Ukraine. Our interests include transport systems, space exploration, 3D modeling, simulation, and data analysis. We joined NASA Space Apps to learn, collaborate, and turn open data into practical ideas. We welcome curious teammates with skills in programming, GIS, data visualization, or design. Enthusiasm and teamwork matter most!
summary:
Marswalk Planner is an interactive prototype for planning scientific expeditions on Mars. Using a HiRISE digital terrain model (DTM) of Jezero Crater, it helps users select scientific objectives, identify candidate exploration sites, and generate routes combining pressurized rover traverses with on-foot EVAs.
The software compares alternative routes based on travel time, terrain risk, energy consumption, subject to crew safety constraints. Users can adjust mission parameters and recalculate routes to explore trade-offs between efficiency and safety.
Developed by Team Space Beatles, Marswalk Planner demonstrates how NASA's open data can support future human exploration of Mars and provide practical applications for transportation engineering and mission planning.
details:
Our Solution

Marswalk Planner is an interactive mission-planning application designed to support future human exploration of Mars. It combines science target selection, rover navigation, walking EVA planning, and crew safety assessments in one system.

How It Works

The user selects a scientific goal and a specific research task. The application analyzes available terrain data, identifies potentially suitable and accessible research sites, and proposes up to five candidate destinations.

For a selected destination, the planner calculates a route from the expedition base to a rover staging location, followed by a walking EVA to the scientific target and a return traverse.

The system compares three planning scenarios: Fastest, Safest, and a simplified Two-Rover Support scenario.

Users can modify mission parameters, including rover mobility, allowable slopes, energy reserves, EVA duration, environmental conditions, and safety requirements. The application recalculates routes and reports their estimated performance.

Data and Technology

Our prototype uses an actual HiRISE digital terrain model of Jezero Crater, developed from NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter observations and published by the USGS.

Terrain elevation is used to calculate slopes, roughness, potential obstacles, and line-of-sight (LOS) visibility.

The software combines fuzzy risk assessment, graph-based shortest-path algorithms, rover energy calculations, and simplified models of on-foot traverse performance and consumable limits.

The application was developed using Python, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, Rasterio, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Innovation and Benefits

Our approach integrates transportation engineering principles with planetary exploration. Instead of simply displaying a map or finding the shortest route, Marswalk Planner evaluates how scientific objectives and crew safety constraints influence route selection.

The prototype makes these trade-offs visible and allows users to investigate alternative mission scenarios interactively.

Current Limitations

The terrain model is based on actual NASA mission data, while several environmental and vehicle parameters are modeled or estimated.

Six scientific tasks are currently available using the observational terrain dataset. Additional tasks require spectral or geological data that have not yet been integrated.

The Two-Rover Support scenario is simplified, and the resulting routes require further validation before any operational use.

Future Development

Planned improvements include integrating THEMIS thermal inertia and CRISM mineralogical data, validating routing models against actual rover traverses, and supporting longer multi-sol expeditions.

The project can also serve as an educational tool for transport engineering, planetary science, and mission planning.
